overview.description: CRISPR uses a short guide RNA to direct a Cas enzyme to a ~20 nt target adjacent to a PAM, where it cuts DNA. Repair by NHEJ yields knockouts; an HDR template yields precise edits. The art is choosing a unique target and minimising off-targets.
objectives: design a specific ~20 nt gRNA with a valid PAM

steps.description: CRISPR uses a short guide RNA to direct a Cas enzyme to a ~20 nt target adjacent to a PAM, where it cuts DNA. Repair by NHEJ yields knockouts; an HDR template yields precise edits. The art is choosing a unique target and minimising off-targets.
steps.intro: CRISPR uses a short guide RNA to direct a Cas enzyme to a ~20 nt target adjacent to a PAM, where it cuts DNA. Repair by NHEJ yields knockouts; an HDR template yields precise edits. The art is choosing a unique target and minimising off-targets.

instructions.title: Define the edit
instructions.description: Decide knockout (no template) vs precise edit (HDR template).

instructions.title: Design the gRNA
instructions.description: Pick a unique ~20 nt target next to a PAM; score on-/off-target with a design tool.

instructions.title: Clone the guide
instructions.description: Insert the gRNA oligos into a Cas9 plasmid (often via Golden Gate).

instructions.title: Deliver & validate
instructions.description: Deliver the Cas9+gRNA into cells and validate the edit by sequencing.

submission.description: Design a validated gRNA (with PAM and off-target assessment) and outline your knockout or knock-in strategy.
